claims.text: Short-range chemical clustering forms during synthesis in the selected HEA.
Short-range chemical clustering enhances local electron-phonon coupling.
The clustering-enhanced electron-phonon coupling triggers superconductivity below a critical temperature.
The as-synthesized selected HEA has a disordered atomic distribution.
Controlled annealing can alter the degree of local chemical clustering.
Adjusting elemental ratios can promote or suppress local chemical clustering.
The controlled comparison will vary local chemical ordering while keeping the samples' macroscopic structure comparable.
Ambient-pressure measurements isolate intrinsic microstructural effects.
Local chemical clusters or short-range ordered regions modify the local bonding environment.
A threshold cluster density or cluster size exists above which electron-phonon coupling becomes sufficient for Cooper pairing.
Samples with enhanced clustering will have a higher superconducting critical temperature than the as-synthesized baseline.
Samples with enhanced clustering will show a more robust zero-resistance state than the baseline.
Enhanced clustering will produce vibrational-mode shifts indicative of stronger electron-phonon interactions.
The as-synthesized, fully disordered baseline has no or weak superconducting behavior.
The relevant superconducting behavior is expected below approximately 10 K.
The proposed mechanism should apply only while compositional changes do not induce a phase transformation or gross structural change.
TEM or XRD measurements can quantify the degree of local chemical clustering.
Failure of enhanced clustering to correlate with increased Tc, stronger zero-resistance behavior, or increased electron-phonon-coupling signatures would falsify the proposed clustering mechanism.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis says that short-range clusters form during synthesis, whereas the as-synthesized initial state and baseline are described as disordered or fully disordered.
The initial state's superconducting behavior is described as uncharacterized, but the baseline is asserted to show no or weak superconductivity.
